name: Saroj Rani Gupta
forbes_bio: Saroj Rani Gupta cofounded APL Apollo Tubes in 1986 with her late husband S.K. Gupta. It was initially called Bihar Tubes.
Delhi-based APL Apollo Tubes is a leading producer of a range of widely used, branded steel products.
Her son, Sanjay Gupta, runs the company as managing director.

name: Lillian Teh Li Ming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Lilian Teh Li Ming is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: Sergey Shishkarev
forbes_bio: Sergey Shishkarev is the founder Delo Group, one of Russia's largest transport and logistics companies, which he started in 1993.
Delo's core asset is DeloPorts, which owns several terminals in the Novorossiysk sea port.
In 2019, state-owned conglomerate Rosatom bought a 30% stake in Delo. Since then Shishkarev has made several mergers and acquisitions to expand the business.
Shishkarev started Delo as a logistics and port management company. It's since become a major domestic player in the transportation industry with interests in sea terminals, rail cars and ships.
In 2022 Delo acquired shipping company SASCO and a stake in Maersk's Global Ports, Russia's largest container operator.

name: Nikesh Arora
sec_insider_companies: Palo Alto Networks Inc (PANW) - Chief Executive Officer; Uber Technologies, Inc (UBER) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun India (2019); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Nikesh Arora has been chairman and CEO of cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks since 2018.
The firm's stock has soared under Arora's leadership, making both him and the company's founder, Nir Zuk, billionaires.
Arora has netted nearly $800 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares since 2023.
He previously worked at Google for nearly a decade, where he rose to chief business officer, before leaving for Japanese investment giant SoftBank in 2014.
Arora was promoted to president and chief operating officer of SoftBank in 2015 and touted as the likely successor to the firm's billionaire founder Masayoshi Son.
Things didn't go as planned, and Arora resigned from SoftBank in 2016. He ended up cashing out at least $360 million (before taxes) during his short stint at the company.

name: Xu Chuanhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014); Hurun China (2005-2018)
forbes_bio: Xu Chuanhua founded a small family workshop to produce liquid soap and detergent in 1986 when he was 52 years old.
Today, his Transfar Group generates most of its business from logistics and chemicals. It also operates in agribusiness and investment industries.
Xu has retired from daily operations, handing reins to sons Guanju and Guanbao, who are chairman and vice chairman of Transfar Group respectively.

name: Peter Done
appears_on: Hurun Global (2019); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)

name: Zuo Yuyu
forbes_bio: Zuo Yuyu is founder and chairman of Leader Harmonious Drive Systems, which makes harmonic reducers - the "joints" of robots.
Known also as Leaderdrive, the Suzhou-based company is China's largest manufacturer of harmonic reducers by market cap, with customers such as domestic humanoid company UBTech Robotics.
In February 2026, Leaderdrive agreed to set up a joint venture with Taiwan's auto-parts supplier Minth Group in the U.S. to develop joint modules for humanoids.
Yuyu founded Leaderdrive in 2011 with the aim of making more affordable robotics components.
His brother Jing serves as Leaderdrive's vice chairman.

name: Chris Wanstrath
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2020); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026)
forbes_bio: Chris Wanstrath cofounded software development platform GitHub in 2008.
Microsoft acquired the company for $7.5 billion in an all-stock deal in 2018. Wanstrath was the firm's largest individual shareholder.
In 2023, he cofounded a "developer-friendly" indie video game publisher called Null.
He serves on the board of the Computer History Museum in Mountain View, CA.

name: Chris Ellison
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Chris Ellison is a veteran of the Australian mining sector, who draws his wealth from a minority stake in listed Mineral Resources.
The company mines both iron ore and a mineral called spodumene, which contains lithium.
In 2021, Mineral Resources together with U.S. lithium giant Albemarle re-opened the Wodinga mine in the Pilbara, in north-west Australia. It holds 29% of the world's spodumene.
Ellison was appointed non-executive chairman of lithium explorer Delta Lithium in September 2023, after Mineral Resources increased its stake to 23%.
Ellison grew up in a poor family in rural New Zealand where his father was a pig farmer and later worked in a quarry.
forbes_facts: Ellison is New Zealand's honorary consul in the state of western Australia.
Ellison bought fellow mining billionaire Angela Bennett's riverside home in 2009 for A$ 57.5 million.

name: Ruan Hongliang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026)
forbes_bio: Ruan Hongliang is founder and chairman of Flat Glass Group, a manufacturer of specialized glass products used in solar power.
Ruan started the company in 1998 and is now dual-listed in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
Ruan's wife Jiang Jinhua serves as Flat's vice chairman; daughter Ruan Zeyun rose to president in 2023.

name: Zhang Liaoyuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020); Hurun Global (2020-2022); Hurun China (2019-2021)
forbes_bio: Zhang Liaoyuan is the chairman of Chinese snack food company Three Squirrels.
Three Squirrels raised $85 million in a China IPO in 2019 and started trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on July 12.
Zhang worked an electrician before he entered the nut, seeds and dried fruit business in 2003.
Zhang owns 53% of Three Squirrels.
